content: Probenecid is prescribed to treat chronic gout and gouty arthritis. It is used to prevent gout attacks but is not effective in treating an attack once it has started. This medication works by acting on the kidneys to help the body eliminate uric acid. Additionally, Probenecid is sometimes used to enhance the effectiveness of certain antibiotics by preventing their excretion in the urine. If you have questions about other uses of this medication, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Probenecid is available in tablet form and is taken orally. For chronic gout or gouty arthritis, it is typically taken twice daily. When used with antibiotics to increase their effectiveness, it is usually taken four times daily. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take Probenecid exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it or take it more frequently than prescribed. During the first 6 to 12 months of treatment, Probenecid may increase the frequency of gout attacks, but it will eventually help prevent them. Your doctor may prescribe another medication, such as colchicine, to reduce this effect. Before taking Probenecid, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to Probenecid or any other drugs. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially aminosalicylic acid, antibiotics, aspirin, cancer chemotherapy agents (e.g., methotrexate), clofibrate (Atromid-S), dapsone, diflunisal (Dolobid), diuretics (water pills), heparin, indomethacin (Indocin), anxiety medications, nitrofurantoin (Macrodantin, Macrobid), oral diabetes medications, pyrazinamide, salsalate (Disalcid), and vitamins. Avoid aspirin products while taking Probenecid, as they may interfere with its effectiveness. If you need a pain or fever reliever, ask your doctor or pharmacist to recommend an aspirin substitute, such as acetaminophen (Tylenol). Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had ulcers, kidney stones, kidney disorders, or blood disorders. Let your doctor know if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking Probenecid, contact your doctor immediately. Inform your doctor if you plan to undergo surgery involving general anesthesia. If you are undergoing urine tests, notify your doctor and laboratory personnel that you are taking Probenecid, as it may affect test results. While taking Probenecid, drink at least six to eight full glasses of water daily to prevent kidney stones, unless otherwise directed by your doctor. If Probenecid causes an upset stomach, take it with food or antacids. If you miss a dose of Probenecid, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Probenecid may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following mild side effects and they persist or worsen: headache, upset stomach, vomiting, loss of appetite, or dizziness. If you experience severe side effects, such as a severe skin rash, difficulty breathing or swallowing, or unusual bleeding or bruising, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store Probenecid in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor will order specific lab tests to monitor your response to Probenecid. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
